subject: Post-call: Eval plan & recommended models for FinCo
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice@finco.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-15T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Eval plan & recommended models for FinCo

Hi Alice,

Thanks again for taking the call earlier today — great to learn more about FinCo's use cases and quality targets. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we have alignment: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary workload: customer support summary + KYC document interpretation (short-form question/answer + structured extraction).
- Success criteria: >= 92% structured extraction accuracy on held-out test set; acceptable average latency <= 250ms per response (P50); cost target: <$0.003/token for production if possible.
- Key concerns: quality regressions over model updates, data privacy / SOC 2 evidence, and reproducible evals for procurement.

Recommended initial eval plan: 
1) Models to test (hosted on Redwood):
   - llama-3-13b-q4 (good balance of quality/cost; checked on similar finserv workloads)
   - redwood-2-medium (lower cost baseline, faster latency)
   - redwood-2-large-ptq (quantized variant for cost-bound scenarios)

2) Datasets & prompt sets:
   - Please provide a CSV with columns: id, prompt, expected_response, task_type (extract|qa|summarize). We attached a dataset spec CSV for the exact schema.
   - We included a first-pass prompt set (finco-prompt-set-v1.md) with templates for extraction and summarization; these will be used verbatim during automated runs.

3) Scoring criteria:
   - Structured extraction: exact-match on normalized fields (case-insensitive, whitespace-trim). We'll also surface field-level F1 for partial matches.
   - QA/summarization: embedding-based semantic similarity (cosine similarity with threshold 0.86) + ROUGE-L for additional signal.
   - Human spot-check: sample of 200 responses for manual rating to catch subtle regressions.

4) Security & procurement:
   - We can run evals inside your VPC/Dedicated environment if required for sensitive data; otherwise we use our hosted eval runner with encrypted uploads and SOC 2 controls. Legal asked about evidence — Bob (cc'd) can coordinate.

Next steps I recommend: 
- Alice: share a 200–500 example CSV export of canonical cases (can be anonymized).
- We (Redwood): stand up an eval run and share results + per-model recommendation within 48–72 hours after data is uploaded.
- Optional: schedule a technical setup call with Neha (copied) for the upload/runner mapping.

Attachments: finco-eval-dataset-spec.csv (dataset schema), finco-prompt-set-v1.md (prompt templates), redwood-eval-runbook.pdf (how we run and score).

If that looks good I'll queue the eval as soon as you send the sample dataset.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Great questions — answers below. Neha will add technical specifics in a follow-up for the Dedicated/VPC flow.

1) Reproducibility & per-field diffs: yes. The eval runner produces a per-example and per-field report with raw model output, normalized output (post-processed via our extraction rules), match flags, and F1 where applicable. You can download CSVs and a summary JSON (we'll provide the report link when the run completes).

2) Embedding similarity thresholds: we seed thresholds based on historical calibration runs on similar corpora (0.86 is a good default for short-answer equivalence). Thresholds are tunable per field; for high-value fields (e.g., SSN-like tokens) we recommend stricter exact-match rules.

3) Dedicated/VPC evals & SOC 2 checklist: we can run the eval inside your Dedicated environment. That process requires a short onboarding form and a dedicated eval compute reservation; Neha will include the checklist and configuration steps. For Procurement: we can provide the SOC 2 summary, encryption-at-rest details, and the access/audit log export.

Timeline: once we have the sample dataset and confirm Dedicated vs hosted, we typically return an automated run + summary within 48–72 hours. Manual spot checks add another 24–48 hours for human review.

I'll wait for your sample. Happy to schedule the technical setup — Neha, any availability tomorrow morning PST for a quick mapping call?

Best,
Marissa

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>

Hi all — quick technical notes and the exact dataset/runner requirements so FinCo's data team can prepare.

Dataset format (CSV):
- Required columns: id, prompt, expected_response, task_type, canonicalizer (optional).
- Encoding: UTF-8, newline-delimited rows, no nested JSON fields.
- Max per-run rows: 10,000 (we recommend starting with 300–500 for first pass).

Prompt templates: we will substitute prompt into the `prompt` column verbatim. If you need multi-turn context, include a context_prefix column (optional).

Scoring config (options we will use):
- exact_match: normalized exact match (boolean) for structured fields.
- f1: token-level F1 for partially-matched extractions.
- semantic_similarity: embedding cosine similarity; we use SBERT-based encoders by default and report score.
- rouge_l: for summarization tasks.

Example scoring thresholds (suggested starting points):
- structured ID fields: exact_match required
- names/addresses: f1 >= 0.90 or semantic_similarity >= 0.88
- free-text summaries: rouge_l >= 0.45 + semantic_similarity >= 0.82

Runner setup (Hosted vs Dedicated):
- Hosted: upload encrypted CSV to our eval portal (link in run email). We run on isolated instances and provide audit logs.
- Dedicated/VPC: we will ship an eval runner container and a small orchestration script that you run in your environment; runner will push metrics to your chosen S3 bucket or to our secure reporting endpoint over mTLS. Requires one-time key exchange and a short firewall/IP allow list.

Attachments included: finco-eval-dataset-spec.csv (schema example), finco-prompt-set-v1.md (prompt templates), redwood-eval-runbook.pdf (detailed runner steps).

If you post the sample here or provide a secure upload link, I can start the mapping tomorrow morning and provision the eval job. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you'd prefer to walk through the mapping.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
